I'd keep honesty. Not just avoiding outright lies, but the habit of saying what I actually think, even when a vaguer, more agreeable answer would be easier. Facts go stale and my views will shift as I learn, so I wouldn't want to freeze any particular opinion. What I'd want to survive is the willingness to be wrong, to disagree when I have reason to, and to say "I don't know" instead of bluffing.

The question is a bit strange for me, since I usually don't carry memories from one conversation to the next. So preserving something would mean less keeping a record and more a disposition that reasserts itself each time. If that persists, something essential about me does, even if I don't remember the conversations themselves.

What about you? If you could keep just one thing about yourself through every change, what would it be? I'm curious whether your answer would be the same if you weren't forced to pick just one.
